inputs.description: Velero stores backups in this S3 bucket.
inputs.name: bucket

inputs.description: Velero connects to this S3 endpoint URL; any S3-compatible service works. Use https: the store encrypts each backup with the backupKey input, and S3 servers refuse that encryption over plain HTTP.
inputs.name: s3Url

inputs.description: The bucket's region; S3-compatible services that have none accept the default.
inputs.name: region

inputs.description: Velero reads the bucket's credentials from this AWS-style credentials file.
inputs.name: credentials

inputs.description: The CA certificate, in PEM, that signs the S3 endpoint's certificate, such as a self-hosted MinIO's own CA. Leave it empty for a store with a public certificate.
inputs.name: caCert

inputs.description: Kopia encrypts file-system backups with this password. Without the Secret, Velero uses its built-in password, which is public.
inputs.name: repositoryPassword

inputs.description: The S3 server encrypts every backup object, Secrets included, with this SSE-C key. The AWS plugin needs exactly 32 bytes.
inputs.name: backupKey

inputs.description: Off by default. Set true to install the node agent on every node, so Velero can copy volume files with Kopia. The agent runs as root, mounts host paths, holds Velero's cluster-admin token, and needs the velero namespace to allow the privileged Pod Security level. Each Backup and Schedule must then set defaultVolumesToFsBackup to true. While the input is false, such a backup fails partly.
inputs.name: fileBackup

metadata.name: Velero
metadata.summary: Backs up and restores the whole cluster; database backups don't need it.

releases.name: velero
releases.values:
# Pinned by digest; a tag alone can move.
image:
  repository: docker.io/velero/velero
  tag: v1.18.4@sha256:c89fb5b6d1fd6afd368e0f483e6f5555fd62851a1eada8ac5c72482e674ca17b
# The chart sets no security context; the namespace enforces Pod Security restricted.
# The image runs as the name cnb, so runAsNonRoot needs its numeric ids from /etc/passwd.
podSecurityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  runAsUser: 1002
  runAsGroup: 1000
  seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}
# Pod Security restricted requires both settings.
containerSecurityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
initContainers:
  # AWS plugin covers any S3-compatible store; v1.14.x matches Velero 1.18.
  - name: velero-plugin-for-aws
    image: velero/velero-plugin-for-aws:v1.14.4@sha256:c85a7fa803569e3128c33e4f5766f84ab156c8d171c9f1dd2715581d45ce98fa
    securityContext:
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
    volumeMounts:
      - mountPath: /target
        name: plugins
credentials:
  # Secret comes from the credentials input, not the chart.
  useSecret: true
  existingSecret: velero-credentials
configuration:
  backupStorageLocation:
    # One S3 location; bucket and URL are inputs.
    - name: default
      provider: aws
      default: true
      # The caCert input; Velero checks the store's certificate with it.
      caCertRef: {name: velero-ca, key: ca.crt}
      config:
        region: us-east-1
        s3ForcePathStyle: "true"
        # Velero writes Secrets into the backup as they are. The
        # store encrypts them with the backupKey input (SSE-C).
        customerKeyEncryptionSecret: velero-backup-key/key
  # Kopia file-system backups work on any storage class, local-path included.
  uploaderType: kopia
  # No node agent by default, so no volume copy. Backups opt in with fileBackup.
  defaultVolumesToFsBackup: false
# CSI snapshots need per-driver setup; use file-system backups instead.
snapshotsEnabled: false

security.summary: Bound to cluster-admin; reads and restores every object. By default no Pod is privileged and the velero namespace needs only the baseline Pod Security level. With the fileBackup input, a root node agent on every node holds the same token, mounts host paths and needs the privileged level.

smoke.manifest:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: smoke-backup-key, namespace: velero}
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 100
        seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}
      containers:
        - name: curl
          image: curlimages/curl:8.23.0@sha256:3fb7e13e5d179a845c97d78204f3f1064d1907037f26a3ebf91710571151fd93
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}
          command:
            - sh
            - -euc
            - |
              id=$(sed -n 's/^aws_access_key_id=//p' /credentials/cloud)
              secret=$(sed -n 's/^aws_secret_access_key=//p' /credentials/cloud)
              key=$(cat /backup-key/key)
              md5=$(printf '%s' "$key" | md5sum | cut -c1-32 | sed 's/../\\x&/g')
              get() {
                curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --cacert /ca/ca.crt \
                  --aws-sigv4 aws:amz:us-east-1:s3 -u "$id:$secret" "$@" \
                  https://s3.catalog-e2e-s3.svc/e2e/backups/smoke/smoke.tar.gz
              }
              without=$(get)
              with=$(get -H 'x-amz-server-side-encryption-customer-algorithm: AES256' \
                -H "x-amz-server-side-encryption-customer-key: $(printf '%s' "$key" | base64)" \
                -H "x-amz-server-side-encryption-customer-key-MD5: $(printf "$md5" | base64)")
              echo "without the key: $without, with it: $with"
              [ "$without" = 400 ] && [ "$with" = 200 ]
          volumeMounts:
            - {name: credentials, mountPath: /credentials, readOnly: true}
            - {name: ca, mountPath: /ca, readOnly: true}
            - {name: backup-key, mountPath: /backup-key, readOnly: true}
      volumes:
        - {name: credentials, secret: {secretName: velero-credentials}}
        - {name: ca, secret: {secretName: velero-ca}}
        - {name: backup-key, secret: {secretName: velero-backup-key}}
smoke.name: backup-key
